freight.description: The Freight Transportation Services Index is at 135.7 (-2.0% vs a year ago): freight volumes are softening. This index tracks the physical volume of for-hire freight moved across trucking, rail, inland waterways, pipelines, and air cargo — a measure of whether goods are actually moving, not what they cost. Blended with a daily transportation-sector equity proxy (IYT @ $81.76, 2026-10-22 00:00:00) at 30% weight so this category moves between monthly BTS prints (which carry a 1-2 month publication lag).
freight.calculation: Score = 72 + YoY% × 6.5, clipped 0-100. Contracting freight volume (negative YoY) lowers the score; steady or growing volume reads healthy. Updated monthly by the BTS (1-2 month lag). Blended 70%/30% with a daily IYT transportation-equity proxy scored by direct percentile.

supply_chain.source: NY Fed GSCPI + BDRY daily proxy
supply_chain.description: GSCPI at +1.28 standard deviations from its historical average: supply chain pressures are well above normal. For context, the Weekly Economic Index is at +3.33 (macro activity, not scored). Blended with a daily dry-bulk freight-rate proxy (BDRY @ $12.65, 2026-10-22 00:00:00) at 30% weight so this category moves between monthly GSCPI prints.
supply_chain.calculation: Score = 50 - GSCPI × 12.5, clipped 0-100 (GSCPI is a z-score, 0 = average pressure, monthly from the NY Fed), blended 70%/30% with a daily BDRY dry-bulk freight-rate proxy scored by inverse percentile.

energy.description: WTI crude is $99.46/bbl and US retail diesel is $6.28/gal. This category blends both legs of the oil complex into one fuel-cost-pressure gauge. It measures energy cost pressure on supply chains, not demand-side health.
energy.calculation: Score = average of two inverse percentiles (crude price and diesel price, each within its trailing 730-day FRED distribution). Cheaper than most of the window = high score (low cost pressure).

tariffs.description: Trade Policy Uncertainty (categorical EPU) is at 1212.9. This index counts newspaper coverage of trade policy uncertainty specifically — tariffs, trade wars, import/export policy — rather than general economic policy noise. Updated monthly.
tariffs.calculation: Score = inverse percentile of the latest value within the trailing 730-day range. Higher trade policy uncertainty = lower score.

geopolitical.description: Analyzed recent supply chain news. Found 3 high-severity and 2 medium-severity risk events affecting the score.
geopolitical.calculation: News score = 100 + sum of the 10 most severe negative article severities (RSS + VADER; deduplicated by title, total deduction floored at -60).

weather.description: Real-time weather analysis of 37 of 37 major shipping ports. Currently tracking 0 locations with suboptimal operating conditions.

aero_metals.description: IMF global aluminum is $3,158/metric ton and nickel is $16,632/mt. Aerospace airframes and superalloys are aluminum- and nickel-intensive; this is a cost-pressure gauge, not a demand gauge. Blended with COMEX aluminum futures (ALI=F $3092) at 30% weight so this category moves between monthly IMF prints.
aero_metals.calculation: Score = average of two inverse percentiles (aluminum, nickel) within the trailing 730-day window, blended 30% with COMEX aluminum futures scored against their own 2-year range. Cheaper than most of the window = high score.

aero_orders.description: Census manufacturers' new orders for nondefense aircraft and parts are $18,825 million this month ($18,686M as a 3-month average). Higher order books read healthier. The average exists because a single widebody order can dominate one monthly print.
aero_orders.calculation: Score = direct percentile of the 3-month average of ANAPNO within the trailing 730-day window. Higher orders = higher score.

aero_production.description: Federal Reserve industrial production for aerospace product and parts (NAICS 3364) is 99.3 (index 2017=100). This measures real output at US aerospace plants, not orders or prices. Higher production reads healthier.
aero_production.calculation: Score = direct percentile of IPG3364S within the trailing 730-day window. Higher output = higher score.

aero_ppi.description: Aircraft manufacturing PPI (PCU336411336411) is 304.7, +2.7% year-over-year. This is a cost-pressure gauge of inflation, not the index level: a high but slowing PPI is less stressful than accelerating producer prices. Faster PPI growth squeezes airframe and engine supply chains.
aero_ppi.calculation: Score = inverse percentile of the year-over-year change in PCU336411336411 within the trailing 730-day window. Slower PPI inflation = higher score. The index level is not ranked — a steadily rising PPI would otherwise pin at 0.

chip_fab_util.description: Advanced nodes (≤7nm) = 69% of wafer revenue. Supply-constrained.

chip_memory_prices.description: HBM pricing at $16/GB in 2026 (≈+20% renewals). Healthy moderate pricing.
chip_memory_prices.calculation: Bell-curve score centered at $15/GB, extremes penalized

chip_lead_times.description: Average lead time of 38 weeks for key components (CoWoS-L, CoWoS-S, CoWoS-S, CoWoS-L, CoWoS-L, CoWoS-S, TSMC N3, TSMC N3, TSMC N3) in Q2 2024, Jun 2024, Q4 2024, Q4 2024, Q1 2026, Q1 2026, Q2 2024, Q4 2024, Q1 2026

chip_wafer_prices.description: TSMC TSMC pricing at $16,500 per wafer in 5nm (2020).
